data.title: Bitcoin Higher After Weekend Dip Buyers Prevent Further Slide
data.description:
By Joseph Wilkins

Bitcoin recovered some ground on Monday after a bruising weekend that saw the flagship cryptocurrency fall to its lowest level in over two years.

Bitcoin was 1% higher at $61,536, recovering after tumbling as low as $55,691 during Saturday's session. Ether was 0.2% higher at $1,718 after a steep fall to $1,560 over the weekend.

Cryptocurrencies and stocks were pressured last week as the AI trade sold off heavily. Bitcoin's relationship with equities has overtaken gold and the dollar as the strongest macro driver in November, Citi's Alex Saunders said. "Bitcoin's three-month correlation with the S&P 500 has risen above its correlation with gold, which has eased but remains positive, while the relationship with the dollar has become less negative," he wrote.

The issue, Saunders added, is that the selloff in crypto has been far larger than the decline in the S&P 500, meaning higher correlation has not translated into a similar magnitude of price action.

Citi lowered its 12-month bitcoin forecast to $99,532 from $113,000 last week on lower exchange-traded fund demand and a tighter macroeconomic backdrop.

Dip buyers were willing to return to bitcoin when the price fell to near $55,000, said Linh Tran at multiasset broker XS.com. But expectations of interest-rate hikes, a still-strong dollar and continued ETF outflows keep the outlook cautious. Over the next few sessions, Tran said he expects bitcoin to trade around $60,000.

data.title: Morning Bid: AI, caramba!
data.description:
MORNING BID: AI, CARAMBA!

It's been a bruising November for the AI faithful, with markets from Taiwan and South Korea to the US staring at steep monthly losses as the selloff in tech and chip stocks at the heart of the AI boom shows little sign of letting up.

Investors are questioning whether vast sums of mostly borrowed money spent building data centres to power AI tools will generate returns fast enough to repay lenders or big enough to justify some of the high stock prices.

Add to that the departure of Nvidia's influential figurehead Jensen Huang, an intensifying US-China tech war and the prospect of greater scrutiny over the data centre buildout following the Democrats' sweeping midterm victory, and the AI trade is looking increasingly shaky.

US futures bounced on Monday following last week's wipeout but selling pressure remained in Asia, with trading thinned by a holiday in Japan.

The scale of the selloff has once again caught the attention of policymakers in South Korea and Taiwan — the region's AI bellwethers.

South Korea's finance minister on Monday reiterated plans to stabilise the market, if necessary. Taiwan's financial regulator has ordered a tightening of short-selling rules for stocks, while in China, stock exchanges announced a batch of support measures such as easing requirements for margin financing.

As Goldman Sachs' Tony Pasquariello puts it: "The market has shown its hand regarding its dependency on the AI story.

"After nearly four years of uninterrupted advancement — during which time the AI theme was rocket fuel for the market and, thus, the wealth effect — we've entered a far more complicated period."

The next key catalyst that could determine whether the selloff snowballs further will be Wednesday's release of the US personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index, a key inflation gauge that could offer clues on how much further the Federal Reserve may need to raise rates.

Expectations of a 25-basis-point Fed hike next month have kept the dollar perched near a 19-month high, with the global stocks rout lending the greenback an additional safe-haven bid.

Separately, MSCI CEO Henry Fernandez conveyed a willingness to consider alternatives to a two-step downgrade of Indonesia's stock-market status in recent talks with President Prabowo Subianto, Bloomberg News reported, citing people with knowledge of the discussion.

Key developments that could influence markets on Monday:

- France, Germany, euro zone S&P flash manufacturing, services PMI (November)

- UK flash manufacturing, services PMI (November)

- New York Fed President John Williams speaks

(Rae Wee)

THIS ANNOUNCEMENT CONTAINS INSIDE INFORMATION

Drax Group plc

(“Drax”, “the Group”, “Drax Group”, “the Company”; Symbol: DRX)

Trading update and CMD with earnings upgrades

Trading update – highlights

  • Strong system support and generation performance since September
  • Full year 2026 expectations for Adj. EBITDA(1) significantly above current consensus(2)
  • Additional merchant biomass generation added for summer 2027
  • €1bn 5.5-year bond issued, Bluefield Solar Income Fund (BSIF) bridging facility repaid
  • FID taken on three new solar projects (c.130MW) underpinned by 15-year CfD contracts

Capital Markets Day (CMD) – highlights

  • Ambition for double-digit average annual growth rate in earnings and dividends (2027-2031)(3)

- Group Adj. EBITDA of £800-900m in 2029 - existing business and committed developments

- Group Adj. EBITDA of >£1bn in 2031, inclusive of incremental investment in growth

- >12% average CAGR in Adj. EBITDA (2027-31) with higher earnings per share growth rate

- >10% average CAGR in dividend per share (2027-31)

  • Targeting >£3bn (2026-2031) of free cash flow(4), which combined with balance sheet headroom gives >£3.5bn of capital available to be used for:

- c.£1.5bn – BSIF acquisition and existing BESS developments

- >£1bn – available for further investment in Solar & Wind and Flexgen

- c.£0.8bn – returns to shareholders (2026-2031)

  • Moving leverage target to 2.5x Net debt to Adj. EBITDA

- In line with reduced business risk, and debt capacity available at current credit rating

  • Group to become progressively weighted towards Solar & Wind and Flexgen through 2020s

- Targeting >20% increase in MW under management (6.2GW to 7.6GW) (2026-2029) based on

existing portfolio and committed investments

- Opportunity to invest in additional growth, scaling portfolio to c.9GW by 2031

  • Strategic partnership for GW-scale data centre at Drax Power Station

- Agreement to develop partnership with Radiant, Brookfield and Qai

- Provisionally values powered land at c.$1 million/MW across all three phases

Drax Group CEO, Will Gardiner said: “The UK needs energy security and routes for decarbonisation which are affordable, whilst at the same time encouraging investment to support economic growth. Demand for power is expected to double by 2040 and as the share of gas generation reduces, there is an increased need for more generation across the board, including solar and wind, and the dispatchable flexible generation to support those and help keep the lights on when the wind isn’t blowing and the sun isn’t shining.

“Starting from a strong foundation of system critical assets in Drax Power Station and Cruachan Pumped Storage Hydro, the Group is building a scalable portfolio of flexible and renewable generating assets in the UK, designed to benefit from the growth in renewable power and resulting need for flexible assets to support the system.

“The Group is broadening its generation portfolio, resulting in higher earnings quality supported by an integrated trading and optimisation platform designed to capture more value from every megawatt.

“Growth is underpinned by a strong balance sheet and a clear capital allocation policy with a combination of dividend growth and reinvestment at attractive risk-adjusted returns.”

Trading Update

Full year expectations

Reflecting a strong system support and power generation performance in September and October, the Group has added in the region of £50 million to its net contracted power position for 2026, with additional benefits from activity in the Balancing Mechanism. Accordingly, Drax now expects full year expectations for 2026 to be significantly above current analyst consensus for 2026. The delivery of this strong performance reflects the dispatchable nature of the Group’s portfolio, combined with its trading and optimisation capabilities, which has allowed it to operate flexibly to meet the needs of the power system and support energy security. BSIF, acquired in July 2026, is performing in line with expectations. Full year expectations for the Group remain subject to continued good operational performance.

In 2026 the Group expects Net debt to Adj. EBITDA to be towards 2 times, inclusive of the acquisition of BSIF, before reducing to below 2 times by the end of 2027.

Generation contracted power sales

As at 19 November 2026, Drax had over £1 billion of contracted forward power sales between 2026 and 2028 on its Renewables Obligation (RO) biomass, pumped storage and hydro generation assets, with over £800 million of associated ROCs. Since its last update on 18 September 2026, the Group has added 2.5TWh (net) to its position at an average price of c.£158/MWh between 2026 and 2028. This includes c.2TWh of merchant biomass generation in summer 2027, which reflects additional volume above the level specified in the new low-carbon dispatchable CfD agreement.

Results, Reports & Presentations - Drax Global

Development of a larger and broader UK focused generation portfolio

The Group aims to grow its MW under management and create value by using its broad and deep portfolio of asset-backed generation with differentiated trading and optimisation capabilities.

Drax has a broad portfolio of UK-focused flexible and renewable generation assets, of which biomass remains an important but smaller part of the Group. Between 2025 and 2026 the Group increased its MW under management from 4.0GW to 6.2GW with the acquisitions of BSIF and Flexitricity, and the commissioning of the first of three OCGTs, moving from 4 to over 200 generation assets across the UK. Between 2026 and 2029 the Group plans to increase its MW under management by over 20%, from 6.2GW to 7.6GW, based on existing investment commitments in OCGTs, BESS and solar, which are expected to enter service between 2027 and 2028.

Beyond its existing plans for 7.6GW in 2029, the Group is developing a pipeline of further opportunities for growth, as well as assessing inorganic opportunities. The Group expects to support the delivery of its growth plans with cash generated from the existing business and the funding capacity available within its capital allocation policy. The Group believes that this could lead to a portfolio of around 9GW in 2031, with an associated increase in earnings and free cash flow, predominantly from its Solar & Wind and Flexgen businesses.

Upgraded medium-term financial targets

Reflecting a growing demand for power and system support services, the Group has an ambition for Adj. EBITDA of £800-900 million in 2029 based on its existing portfolio and committed investments, rising to >£1 billion in 2031, inclusive of incremental investment in Solar & Wind and Flexgen. Both Adj. EBITDA numbers are inclusive of development expenditure.

This represents an expected average, non-linear CAGR for Adj. EBITDA of >12% pa between 2027(3) and 2031 and an expected higher rate of earnings per share growth over the same period.

Drax aims to grow its dividend per share sustainably by over 10% pa between 2027(3) and 2031.

Improving earnings quality

In 2025, over 80% of the Group’s Adj. EBITDA was derived from Biomass Operations. By 2029, the Group expects that Solar & Wind and Flexgen will represent the majority of Group Adj. EBITDA. Drax aims to continue this transition through 2031, leading to a more balanced earnings mix, with a greater proportion of contracted revenue and reduced risk, whilst retaining exposure to the upside that comes from volatility in merchant power prices.

Leverage target

In 2017, the Group set out a long-term leverage target of around 2x Net debt(10) to Adj. EBITDA, which would work alongside its single site merchant generation model. Today, the Group is a multi-site, multi-technology portfolio with higher quality earnings. Accordingly, Drax will now target long-term leverage of around 2.5x Net debt to Adj. EBITDA, inclusive of leases, provided that additional debt is used to support further growth. Drax believes that this level remains consistent with the Group current credit ratings.

Cashflow

Between 2026 and 2031 the Group expects to generate over £3 billion of free cash flow(4) from its existing portfolio and committed investments. Taken together with a long-term target of 2.5x Net debt to Adj. EBITDA, the Group is targeting >£3.5 billion of capacity to support investment and returns to shareholders.

The Group expects to return c.£0.8 billion to shareholders between 2026 and 2031 through the continuation of its sustainable and growing dividend policy. Taken together with over £0.3 billion returned in 2025 via dividends and share buybacks, the Group expects to return >£1 billion to shareholders between 2025 and 2031, in line with previous guidance.

With attractive opportunities to invest in Solar & Wind and Flexgen, Drax expects its share buyback programme to remain paused.

Of the remainder of the >£3.5 billion, c.£1.5 billion was used in the acquisition of BSIF and existing BESS developments, leaving >£1 billion for further investment in growth (included in the Group’s ambition for Adj. EBITDA of >£1 billion by 2031).

Hurdle rates

Drax will continue to appraise its investment opportunities, against technology-specific hurdle rates based on WACC plus a risk premium.

A GW-scale pipeline of development opportunities to support continued growth

The Group has a GW-scale pipeline of development opportunities in Solar & Wind and BESS, including floors and tolls, which it will assess in line with its capital allocation policy.

In October 2026, Drax made a final investment decision on three new solar projects in northern England, representing c.130MW and an investment of c.£120 million. These developments, which are expected to enter service in 2028, are underpinned by 15-year CfD agreements, providing high-quality earnings into the 2040s.

Drax also remains alert to other inorganic sector opportunities.

Biomass operations

Reflecting the integrated nature of its operations in the US South and biomass generation at Drax Power Station, the Group is combining these activities into a Biomass Operations reporting segment. This segment also includes the Group’s Canadian operations, which are currently under a strategic review.

The Drax Power Station estate – which is located centrally in the UK and next to one of the country’s largest substations – comprises over 1,000 acres and has c.4GW of grid access, with 2.6GW of active dispatchable generation, cooling systems, and proximity to the UK fibre network, making it ideal for the development of a potential data centre, alongside power generation.

Drax believes that the size, flexibility, and location of the site make it an important long-term part of the UK energy system and the Group is focused on options to maximise value from the site. In addition to an AI data centre, Drax is exploring long-term options to utilise multiple generation technologies, including dispatchable power, in addition to its existing biomass generation, which can support UK energy security. As a part the development of long-term options for the site, the Group has formally requested 1.2GW of import capacity from the system operator.

Drax is also developing an option to provide non-generation stability services at Drax Power Station to the electricity grid, from two units that do not currently operate. Historically, stability services, including inertia, were provided by large rotating plant but with a reduction in these types of assets and the rollout of intermittent renewables, the electricity grid has an increasing need for stability assets. Drax expects to continue to develop this option through 2027.

Data centre

In 2026, Drax signed an agreement to develop a strategic partnership with Brookfield and Radiant, Brookfield’s UK-headquartered AI infrastructure platform, to jointly develop, deliver and operate an AI data centre on the Drax Power Station estate.

The partnership will combine Radiant’s AI infrastructure expertise with Drax’s powered land and generation capabilities, with investment capital and operating capabilities provided through a Brookfield-Qai AI infrastructure joint venture.

In aggregate, across three development phases, the project has the potential to deliver GW-scale data centre capacity at Drax Power Station.

The agreement provisionally values powered land across all three phases of the project at c.$1 million/MW.

Drax understands that, during 2026, Radiant, as the project’s commercial partner, has been discussing commercial arrangements and requirements with potential tenants for the first phase of the project. These discussions are ongoing.

Progression of the first phase of the project is subject to the necessary planning approvals, as well as receiving the required regulatory and network approvals from Government and the relevant agencies, in addition to securing an acceptable tenant for the project, negotiation of necessary commercial agreements and each party taking a final investment decision.

Cobra Resources plc

(“Cobra” or the “Company”)

Shadow Rose: A Significant Copper Discovery

Fast-tracked assay returns 111m @ 0.63% copper from just 4 meters to end of hole –

Blue Rose mineralised corridor extended to 3km

Plus

Extensive visual copper within drilling at the Netley Hill copper porphyry target

Cobra (LSE: COBR), a South Australian mineral exploration and development company advancing the Wudinna Rare Earth Project and the Manna Hill Copper Project containing multiple discoveries, announces further significant copper results that contribute favourably to the scale and economic potential of the Shadow Rose discovery at Manna Hill.

The Shadow Rose skarn is now viewed by the Company as a significant copper discovery.

Assays extend the Blue Rose mineralised corridor to almost 3km, whilst slim-line RC drilling at the Netley Hill copper-molybdenum target intersects visual copper mineralisation across a significant footprint.

Highlights:

Blue Rose mineralised corridor – Shadow Rose discovery

  • MHRC0055, drilled 220m west of the Shadow Rose discovery hole intersected:
    • 111m at 0.63% Cu, 0.04 g/t Au from 4m to end of hole, including:
    • 12m at 0.81% Cu, 0.03 g/t Au from 6m, and
    • 58m at 0.85% Cu, 0.04 g/t Au from 36m, including
    • 12m at 1.54% Cu, 0.02 g/t Au from 80m
  • Mineralisation remains open – Mineralisation remains open along strike east and west of the Shadow Rose discovery holes and no limit to the depth extent of mineralisation is yet determined. Further drill investigation will be undertaken in an extension of the current funded programme.   
  • The western extent of mineralisation has been extended a further 450m west of MHRC0055 where MHRC0058 is interpreted to have intersected the hanging wall of Shadow Rose skarn including:
  • 12m at 0.34% Cu, 0.13 g/t Au from 42m, and
  • 6m at 0.14% Cu, 0.03 g/t Au, from 114 to end of hole

Netley Hill Porphyry target

  • Visual indications from Netley Hill drilling – Trace of copper and molybdenum mineralisation recognised visually and pxrf analyses in drill returns from shallow depths in several completed slim-line RC holes - positive geological indicators for a shallow, large scale porphyry system.

Note: Visual observations and pXRF readings in this announcement are preliminary, qualitative and semi-quantitative respectively, and are not a substitute for laboratory assay results. No reliance should be placed on them as an indication of grade, tenor or economic significance. Full notes are set out at the end of this announcement.

Figure 1: Plan detailing received, pending results and further drilling across the Blue Rose mineralisation corridor.

Rupert Verco, Managing Director, commented:

“Intersecting 111 metres at 0.63% copper from just 4 metres downhole is a standout result for Shadow Rose. The combination of encouraging copper grade, a substantial mineralised interval, and shallow depth strengthens our confidence in the discovery and its potential to become an important part of the Manna Hill copper story.

“The Cobra team must be commended for their perseverance and dedication. The work completed across the last twelve months has materially increased the scale and economic potential of the Manna Hill project.

“This result provides a compelling foundation to deliver additional scale to the mineralised system. Establishing how far the mineralisation extends, its geometry and its continuity will be central to understanding the opportunity across the Blue Rose mineralised corridor.

“This is a standout result that adds momentum to our copper exploration programme and reinforces the potential we see at Manna Hill. We look forward to building on this discovery as further results come to hand.”

Follow this link to watch a short video of MD Rupert Verco discussing this announcement: https://investors.cobraplc.com/link/PwNN2r

Further Details

Geological context and background

The current drilling programme has been designed to test for extensions to the Blue Rose mineralised corridor. Before the commencement of this drilling campaign, the strike of mineralisation was defined by drilling across a 1.6km strike. Recent results have increased this strike to just under 3km with further upside possible.

The 111m at 0.63% Cu from just 4 meters depth is the third best hole drilled at the project to date on a grade - meter basis and is one of the first four holes testing the Shadow Rose zone.

Background to the Blue Rose mineralisation corridor

Copper mineralisation at Blue Rose is associated with several porphyry type intrusives that have intersected strata bound, subvertical limestone units. Copper mineralisation occurs as shallow oxides and primary mineralisation is predominantly Chalcopyrite-Magnetite-Pyrite.

  • When Cobra announced the option over the project in August 2025, previous exploration had intersected mineralisation along 1.6km of strike within a calc-silicate skarn containing shallow high-grade intersections including:
  • RABR822: 47m at 2.2% Cu, 0.76 g.t Au from 11m
  • RABR025: 132m @ 0.5% Cu from 8m
  • RABR152: 41m @ 1.64% Cu from 9m
  • Under the option period, Cobra tested areas of the skarn for geological continuity and to evaluate the economic potential. Significant intersections include:
  • MHRC0018: 20m at 0.78% Cu, 0.14 g/t Au from 38m, and 74m at 1.02% Cu, 0.25 g/t Au from 70m
  • MHRC0017:  86m at 0.60% Cu, 0.14 g/t Au from 18m
  • MHRC0013: 62m at 1.0% Cu, 0.08 g/t Au from 62m
  • MHRC0003: 56m at 0.34% Cu from 34m
  • A diamond programme testing depth continuity to mineralisation encountered geological indicators of a much larger porphyry system and delivered intersections including:
  • MHDD002:  
    • 23m at 0.63% Cu, 0.09 g/t Au from 186m, including:
    • 12.4m at 1.01% Cu, 0.13g/t Au from 190m, and
    • 10.5m at 0.38% Cu, 0.02 g/t Au from 297.9m
  • MHDD004:  16.9m at 0.21% Cu from 16.6m, and
    • 36m at 0.39% Cu, 0.05g/t Au from 232m, including:
    • 10m at 0.99% Cu, 0.13 g/t Au, 0.02% Mo from 241.5, and
    • 16.9m at 0.08% Mo from 335.5m
  • Step-out high tempo slim-line RC drilling commenced in September aimed at testing several geological interpretations for additional strata-bound skarn mineralisation. Outcropping exposure and copper anomalism within historical rotary air blast (“RAB”) shallow drilling south of Blue Rose was tested as a possible stratigraphic repeat. Results to date include:
  • MHRC0055 intersected:
    • 111m at 0.63% Cu, 0.04 g/t Au from 4m to eoh including:
    • 12m at 0.81% Cu, 0.03 g/t Au from 6m, and
    • 58m at 0.85% Cu, 0.04 g/t Au from 36m, including
    • 12m at 1.54% Cu, 0.02 g/t Au from 80m
  • MHRC0025, drilled 220m east of MHRC055 intersected:
  • 58m at 0.46% Cu, 0.15 g/t Au from 10m, including:
  • 42m at 0.56% Cu, 0.10 g/t Au from 22m, including:
  • 10m at 1.09% Cu from 24m 
  • MHRC0026, drilled 100m south of MHRC0025 intersected:
    • 22m at 0.48% Cu, 0.02 g/t Au from 10m, including:
    • 12m at 0.7% Cu from 16m, and
    • 10m at 0.22% Cu, 0.06 g/t Au from 66m, and
    • 30m at 0.21% Cu, 0.02 g/t Au from 88m
  • The extended programme shall test the depth of mineralisation continuity intersected in MHRC0055 through step-out drilling. Further holes will also seek to confirm further strike continuity west of MHRC0055 and east of MHRC0025

Figure 2: Plan showing follow-up holes to further test the Shadow Rose discovery

Figure 3: Section 427,825mE highlighting intersection of MHRC0055 at Shadow Rose

Previously reported results from the current programme include:

  • Blue Rose West, the western continuity of Blue Rose mineralisation where the gravity edge anomaly shows structural faulting coincident with a large reversely magnetised anomaly. Intersected mineralisation in MHRC0029 is coincident with strong potassic alteration and does not occur within skarn style mineralisation.
  • Blue Rose West, porphyry type intersection — MHRC0029 intersected:
    • 32m at 0.7% Cu, 0.07 g/t Au from 52m, including:
    • 12m at 1.13% Cu, 0.08 g/t Au from 56m
  • Mineralisation occurs contacting the large magnetic anomaly (Figure 1).
  • This intersection is the most compelling geological indicator to date for a high grade potassic porphyry system owing to:
    • Copper mineralisation extending beyond skarn: copper is intersected in non-skarn host rocks, broadening the exploration potential beyond the previously recognised skarn horizons.
    • Elevated potassium provides a potential alteration vector: The association of copper mineralisation with elevated potassium may reflect potassic alteration, supporting investigation of a broader intrusion-related mineralising system.
    • Spatial association with a substantial magnetic target: Mineralisation occurs adjacent to a large modelled magnetic body interpreted to carry remanent magnetisation. Its relationship to the copper mineralisation represents an important target for further investigation.
    • Potential for a linked skarn–porphyry system: The combination of skarn mineralisation, copper in non-skarn rocks and elevated potassium is consistent with a possible interconnected intrusive–hydrothermal system, including a potential porphyry-style component.
    • Focused follow-up drilling additional drillholes planned to test the modelled magnetic body to determine the possible scale of copper/potassic style mineralisation

Visual observations from Netley Hill drilling

  • Porphyry copper-molybdenum mineralisation has previously been identified at Netley Hill where previous intersections include:
  • NETRP03: 24m at 0.3% Cu, 0.02% Mo from 55m to EOH
  • NETRP17: 7m at 0.5% Cu from 52m to EOH
  • NETRP02: 18m at 0.1% Cu, 0.04% Mo from 55m
  • NETDD001: 350m at 0.1% Cu, 0.015% Mo from surface
  • Seven slim-line RC holes totalling 660m have been completed across a large IP anomaly approximately ~3km in length.
  • Copper oxides, predominantly malachite and azurite where observed in drill returns to depths of approximately 70m.
  • In areas, copper sulphides (chalcopyrite, chalcocite and molybdenite) were present with oxide mineralisation.
  • Whilst assays are required to confirm grade and mineralisation widths, cautionary observations suggest shallow copper mineralisation over an extensive footprint.
  • The intensity of mineralisation increased in drillholes MHRC0065 and MHRC0067 that were drilled on the margins of the IP anomaly, which may provide as a useful targeting tool in defining zones of higher-grade mineralisation.

Figure 4: Netley Hill Drilling Plan – initial observations

Figure 5: Primary Molybdenite mineralisation in MHRC0067

Figure 6: Copper oxide mineralisation within MHRC0065 at 104-106m

Disclaimer: Visual observations and portable X-ray fluorescence (“pXRF”) readings referred to in this announcement are preliminary in nature and should not be considered a substitute for laboratory assay results.

Visual estimates of mineralisation, alteration and sulphide abundance are qualitative observations only and do not represent quantitative estimates of grade or metal content.

pXRF measurements provide indicative, semi-quantitative geochemical information and may be affected by a range of factors including sample heterogeneity, moisture content, particle size, surface condition, matrix effects and instrument calibration. pXRF results have therefore been used principally to assist geological interpretation, identify relative geochemical trends and guide sampling.

No reliance should be placed on visual observations or pXRF readings as an indication of the grade, tenor or economic significance of mineralisation. Representative samples have been submitted, or will be submitted, to an accredited laboratory for quantitative analysis. Laboratory assay results will be reported when available and following completion of appropriate quality assurance and quality control procedures.

Criteria

JORC Code explanation

Commentary

Sampling techniques

  • Nature and quality of sampling (eg cut channels, random chips, or specific specialised industry standard measurement tools appropriate to the minerals under investigation, such as down hole gamma sondes, or handheld XRF instruments, etc). These examples should not be taken as limiting the broad meaning of sampling.
  • Include reference to measures taken to ensure sample representivity and the appropriate calibration of any measurement tools or systems used.
  • Aspects of the determination of mineralisation that are Material to the Public Report.
  • In cases where ‘industry standard’ work has been done this would be relatively simple (eg ‘reverse circulation drilling was used to obtain 1 m samples from which 3 kg was pulverised to produce a 30 g charge for fire assay’). In other cases more explanation may be required, such as where there is coarse gold that has inherent sampling problems. Unusual commodities or mineralisation types (eg submarine nodules) may warrant disclosure of detailed information.

Historic Drilling

  • Historic drill programs have been conducted by multiple companies and methods the historically reported results are being reviewed prior to any broader reporting of results. In general, lab assay results across differing programs show comparable tenors of grade and distribution.

Cobra Resources

RC Drilling (2026)

  • RC drill cuttings were collected from the drill rig cyclone in 1 m intervals in industry standard green bags, with a 2 m representative split from the cyclone collected into a calico bag. The green and calico bags were arranged in rows on site for sampling and assaying.
  • 2 m samples were split using a cone splitter mounted on the drill rig.
  • 2026 January-February samples were submitted to BV Laboratories, Perth for geochemical analysis.

Diamond Drilling (2026)

  • HQ sized diamond core was cut and half core sampled.
  • Sampling was generally kept to 1m intervals but adjusted to honour geological boundaries.
  • 2-4kg half core samples were submitted to ALS Laboratories for geochemical analysis.

Slimline RC and Aircore Drilling (Current Program)

  • RC drill cuttings are being collected from the drill rig cyclone in 1 m intervals in industry standard green bags, with a 2 m representative split from the cyclone collected into a calico bag. The green and calico bags were arranged in rows on site for sampling and assaying.
  • 2 m samples are being split using a cone splitter mounted on the drill rig.
  • Samples are being submitted to ALS Laboratories, Perth for geochemical analysis.
  • The current drill program was intended to be slimline RC drilling. Where difficulties with drilling occurred due to ground conditions, the drilling technique was switched to aircore blade drilling to progress drilling.  The drill type was switched back to slimline RC once ground conditions allowed.

Drilling techniques

  • Drill type (eg core, reverse circulation, open-hole hammer, rotary air blast, auger, Bangka, sonic, etc) and details (eg core diameter, triple or standard tube, depth of diamond tails, face-sampling bit or other type, whether core is oriented and if so, by what method, etc).

Historic Drilling

  • Historic drill methods were predominantly aircore and RC drilling with some diamond drilling reported.

Cobra Resources

RC Drilling

  • Schramm T685 RC rig operated by Bullion Drilling Pty Ltd. The RC drilling was conducted using a 5 ¾-inch hammer. A booster air compressor was used throughout the program.

Diamond Drilling

  • UDR 1000 drill rig operated by MJ Drilling Pty Ltd. The diamond drilling was conducted using HQ sized core from surface (except one hole which re-entered a previously drilled RC hole to continue as a diamond tail).
  • HQ core samples were collected from the diamond drill rig from nominal 3 m drill runs and placed into industry standard core trays. 
  • Where broken ground was intersected, run lengths were reduced as appropriate.

Slimline RC Drilling (Current Program)

  • Slimline RC drilling utilized a 89mm hammer bit, ensuring a 12-15kg sample was collected per meter.
  • AC drilling utilized a 85mm blade bit and a 89mm hammer bit, ensuring a 12-15kg sample was collected per meter.

Drill sample recovery

  • Method of recording and assessing core and chip sample recoveries and results assessed.
  • Measures taken to maximise sample recovery and ensure representative nature of the samples.
  • Whether a relationship exists between sample recovery and grade and whether sample bias may have occurred due to preferential loss/gain of fine/coarse material.

Historic Drilling

  • Recoveries have not been assessed.
  • Drill methods and geological conditions are not expected to promote significant reduced recovery or sample biasing

Cobra Resources

RC Drilling

  • Bulk RC samples were visually assessed and considered to be representative with good recoveries. Recoveries were recorded onsite into Cobras MX Deposit database.
  • Water was intersected in several drillholes. Where outside return was lost and sample recovery reduced. Recovery estimates recorded into the companies database. Shroud tolerance was managed to optimise recovery.
  • No relationship was identified between sample recovery and grade.

Diamond Drilling

  • Core blocks were utilised by the drill contractor to indicate where core loss occurred.
  • Core recovery was measured as part of the RQD logging process and recorded onsite into Cobra's MX Deposit database.
  • No relationship was identified between sample recovery and grade.

Slimline RC & Aircore Drilling (current program)

  • Bulk RC samples are being visually assessed and considered to be representative with good recoveries. Recoveries are being recorded onsite into Cobras MX Deposit database.

Logging

  • Whether core and chip samples have been geologically and geotechnically logged to a level of detail to support appropriate Mineral Resource estimation, mining studies and metallurgical studies.
  • Whether logging is qualitative or quantitative in nature. Core (or costean, channel, etc) photography.
  • The total length and percentage of the relevant intersections logged.

Historic

  • Historic logging has been completed with a number of different geological logging codes. These are being translated into a standardized logging format prior to entry into the Cobra Drillhole Database.

Cobra Resources

  • All holes are qualitatively and quantitatively logged for their entire length by suitably qualified Cobra geologists and recorded onsite into Cobra’s MX Deposit database.
  • Qualitative logging included geology, alteration, mineralisation, weathering etc.
  • Quantitative logging included magnetic susceptibility, structural and RQD measurement recording (for diamond core).
  • Mineral Resources have not been estimated; however, the quality of the logging is expected to be suitable for low-confidence resource estimation purposes.
  • The detail of geological logging is considered sufficient for exploration and resource definition drilling.
  • Logging included visual estimates for copper oxides and sulphides as well as pyrite content
  • All intersections were logged.

Sub-sampling techniques and sample preparation

  • If core, whether cut or sawn and whether quarter, half or all core taken.
  • If non-core, whether riffled, tube sampled, rotary split, etc and whether sampled wet or dry.
  • For all sample types, the nature, quality and appropriateness of the sample preparation technique.
  • Quality control procedures adopted for all sub-sampling stages to maximise representivity of samples.
  • Measures taken to ensure that the sampling is representative of the in situ material collected, including for instance results for field duplicate/second-half sampling.
  • Whether sample sizes are appropriate to the grain size of the material being sampled.

Historic

  • Historic sampling has not been assessed.

Cobra Resources

RC Drilling

  • A Metzke cone split 2m composite sample was collected in a calico bag. A portable XRF unit was used as an initial evaluation of Cu mineralisation.  However, entire holes were sampled.
  • Weights of samples submitted for assay were a nominal 2-3kg Sample size and considered appropriate for the material sampled.

Diamond Drilling

  • HQ diamond core was cut, and half core sampled.  This is considered appropriate for the material sampled.

Slimline RC & Aircore Drilling

  • A cone split 2m composite sample are collected in a calico bag. A portable XRF unit is being used as an initial evaluation of Cu mineralisation.  However, entire holes are being sampled.
  • Weights of samples submitted for assay are a nominal 2-3kg Sample size and considered appropriate for the material sampled.

All Sampling

  • Commercially certified reference material of known copper grades and of suitable matrix were included in the laboratory assay sequence at a rate of 1 per 50 samples.
  • First-split duplicate samples were collected at a rate of 1 per 50 samples.
  • A coarse blank sample was inserted 1 in every 50 samples.
  • The Competent Person considers that the sample size is appropriate to the grain size of the material being sampled.
  • Laboratory processing involved oven drying, crushing and pulverising to obtain a representative sub-sample of the material supplied

Quality of assay data and laboratory tests

  • The nature, quality and appropriateness of the assaying and laboratory procedures used and whether the technique is considered partial or total.
  • For geophysical tools, spectrometers, handheld XRF instruments, etc, the parameters used in determining the analysis including instrument make and model, reading times, calibrations factors applied and their derivation, etc.
  • Nature of quality control procedures adopted (eg standards, blanks, duplicates, external laboratory checks) and whether acceptable levels of accuracy (ie lack of bias) and precision have been established.

Historic

  • Lab certificates for a large number of drill samples have been retained from historic drilling. These certificates will be used for the import of data into Cobra’s drillhole database.

Cobra Resources

RC Drilling

  • All samples were managed for the potential presence of asbestiform mineral fibers namely serpentine and chrysotile.
  • 59 element assays were completed by Bureau Veritas (BV) Laboratories, (analytical method MA101 and MA102) for all drill samples, using a four-acid digest from a 25g sub-sample, and ICP-MS & ICP-AES.
  • Au assays were completed by BV Laboratories (analytical method FA001), 40g fire assay and AAS was undertaken on all samples.
  • Standards and blanks were inserted by Cobra (the company), with no issues observed with sample precision (standards) or bias (blanks).
  • Lab internal blanks and standards were within accepted norms.

Diamond Drilling

  • All samples were managed for the potential presence of asbestiform mineral fibers namely serpentine and chrysotile.
  • 60 element assays were completed by ALS Laboratories, (analytical method ME-MS61r) for all drill core samples, using a four-acid digest from a 0.25g sub-sample, and ICP-MS & ICP-AES.
  • Au assays were completed by ALS Laboratories (analytical method Au-AA26), 50g fire assay and AAS was undertaken on all core samples.
  • Standards and blanks were inserted by Cobra (the company), with no issues observed with sample precision (standards) or bias (blanks).
  • Lab internal blanks and standards were within accepted norms.

Slimline RC & Aircore Drilling

  • All samples are being managed for the potential presence of asbestiform mineral fibers namely serpentine and chrysotile.
  • 48 element assays are being undertaken by ALS Laboratories, (analytical method ME-MS61) for all samples, using a four-acid digest from a 0.25g sub-sample, and ICP-MS & ICP-AES.
  • Au assays will be completed by ALS Laboratories (analytical method Au-AA26), 50g fire assay and AAS was undertaken on all samples.
  • Standards and blanks are being inserted by Cobra (the company), with assessment of results to be undertaken once received.
  • Lab internal blanks and standards will be undertaken and results assessed but Cobra Resources.

Verification of sampling and assaying

  • The verification of significant intersections by either independent or alternative company personnel.
  • The use of twinned holes.
  • Documentation of primary data, data entry procedures, data verification, data storage (physical and electronic) protocols.
  • Discuss any adjustment to assay data.

Historic

  • Reported significant intercepts have been reported to the Australian Stock Exchange in the past.
  • Primary assay data and drill logs for reported holes have been reviewed by Cobra staff.
  • Further migration of historic data into the Cobra drillhole database is underway with validation during this process to be undertaken.

Cobra Resources

  • Significant intercepts were validated and reviewed by at least two Cobra Resource’s Geologists.
  • No twinned holes have been drilled by Cobra Resources.  However, drilling has occurred proximal to historic drilling and confirmed historically reported copper mineralisation.
  • Primary data and drill logs were captured in the field and recorded by Cobra staff, into a digital database (MxDeposit).
  • Assay results have not been adjusted other than the conversion of the ‘<’ symbol to a ‘-‘ for importing into geological database.

Location of data points

  • Accuracy and quality of surveys used to locate drill holes (collar and down-hole surveys), trenches, mine workings and other locations used in Mineral Resource estimation.
  • Specification of the grid system used.
  • Quality and adequacy of topographic control.

Historic

  • Historic Drillholes were recorded with a number of different datums.
  • Validation of the datums used for each program have been conducted and are continuing.
  • The key historic drilling used for planning of the 2026 drill programs have high confidence in the datum used and have been assessed in the field.

Cobra Resources

  • Drill hole locations were determined by handheld GPS with a nominal accuracy of +/- 5 metres.
  • All coordinates and maps presented are in the MGA Zone 54 GDA94 coordinate system.
  • Topographic control is provided by Aerometrex Reigel VQ-780ii Airborne Laser Scanner producing LiDAR digital elevation data at 0.1m accuracy with collar heights extracted from a DTM produced from the LiDAR data.
  • Downhole surveys were undertaken by a multi-shot camera and/or gyro.
  • Magnetic declination for the project area is 8.2 degrees east.

Data spacing and distribution

  • Data spacing for reporting of Exploration Results.
  • Whether the data spacing and distribution is sufficient to establish the degree of geological and grade continuity appropriate for the Mineral Resource and Ore Reserve estimation procedure(s) and classifications applied.
  • Whether sample compositing has been applied.

Historic

  • Historic drilling was variably spaced. The drill spacing was sufficient to define mineralisation trends at the Blue Rose Skarn but not to the extent of defining a resource.

Cobra Resources

RC Drilling

  • RC holes were drilled angled south along heritage cleared ‘drill access tracks’ or adjacent to pastoral tracks.  Holes were designed to assess continuation of historically intersected copper mineralisation laterally and at depth.
  • Two metre composite samples were collected for geochemical analysis.

Diamond Drilling

  • Angled diamond holes were drilled in various orientations, positioned to assess extensions to known mineralisation, in addition to assessing untested prospective zones of the geological model. 
  • Results are indicative and require further drilling to fully assess the significance of the intercept/s.

Slimline RC & Aircore Drilling (current program)

  • Holes are generally drilled angled south along heritage cleared ‘drill access tracks’ or adjacent to pastoral tracks.  There were a couple holes at Blue Rose drilling to the north and the drilling at Anabama Hill and Netley Hill are in various orientations as first pass drill testing.
  • Holes were designed to assess continuation of historically intersected copper mineralisation laterally, and also designed to assess for repeat prospective calc-silicate/skarn lithologies to the south-west and to the north of Blue Rose.
  • Two metre composite samples are being collected for geochemical analysis.

Orientation of data in relation to geological structure

  • Whether the orientation of sampling achieves unbiased sampling of possible structures and the extent to which this is known, considering the deposit type.
  • If the relationship between the drilling orientation and the orientation of key mineralised structures is considered to have introduced a sampling bias, this should be assessed and reported if material.
  • The mineralised skarn unit is orientated approximately east-west, with possible repeated units.
  • Drillholes have generally been vertical or south dipping, perpendicular to the strike of the skarn host unit.
  • Deeper historic drilling has been south dipping.
  • Mineralisation is interpreted to be steeply dipping with limited success to date in identifying a slight north or south dip.
  • Deeper planned drilling is designed to improve the definition of mineralisation control.
  • Further diamond drilling is expected to validate geological interpretations.

Sample security

  • The measures taken to ensure sample security.

Cobra Resources

2026 Drilling

  • No issues with sample security were reported or are expected to have occurred.
  • RC sample bags were tied upon collection and stored in polyweave bags until delivery direct to the assay laboratory by a contracted third-party transport company.
  • Diamond core was stored in industry standard core trays, stacked on pallets and strapped for transport.  A third party contract transport company collected the samples and delivered them to Challenger Geological Services Pty Ltd, where they were cut and sampled.  Sampled material was placed into calico bags, double bagged in green plastic bags in the cause of hazardous fibrous material, and stacked on pallets and wrapped for transport.  These were then transported by a contracted transport company directly to ALS laboratory for geochemical assessment.
  • Slimline RC & Aircore sample bags are being tied upon collection and stored in polyweave bags until delivery direct to the assay laboratory by a contracted third-party transport company or transported by Cobra Resources staff.

Directly to ALS Audits or reviews

  • The results of any audits or reviews of sampling techniques and data.
  • No audits or reviews of sampling techniques or data have been undertaken. 

Appendix 5: Section 2 reporting of exploration results

Criteria

JORC Code explanation

Commentary

Mineral tenement and land tenure status

  • Type, reference name/number, location and ownership including agreements or material issues with third parties such as joint ventures, partnerships, overriding royalties, native title interests, historical sites, wilderness or national park and environmental settings.
  • The security of the tenure held at the time of reporting along with any known impediments to obtaining a licence to operate in the area.
  • Blue Rose is located on EL6009 that is heldby Hamelin Gully Pty Ltd. Manna HillMining Pty Ltd, a subsidiary of CobraResources Plc has exercised its option toacquire Hamelin Gully.
  • The Company announced the exercise of the option on 9 July 2026.
  • A 1% Over Riding Royalty Agreement isregistered between Hamelin Gully andSprington Trust.
  • A Native Title Agreement is in place between the Wilyakali People and HamelinGully Pty Ltd.
  • Cultural heritage surveys have beencompleted over EL6009, clearing proposeddrill sites.

Exploration done by other parties

  • Acknowledgment and appraisal of exploration by other parties.
  • Historic Exploration has been conducted by multiple companies with key work completed by PacMag, Lynas and Giralia Resources.
  • Historic exploration demonstrated the geological environment at Blue Rose and the potential for economic mineralization.
  • Commercially driven decisions and land access challenges (now resolved) were common trends in the history of the project transactions

Geology

  • Deposit type, geological setting and style of mineralisation.

Blue Rose

  • Blue Rose is skarn hosted mineralisation on the margins of the Anabama Granite.
  • Oxide mineralisation is stratabound to the Saddleworth limestone formation.
  • A number of porphyry related intrusions have a spatial relationship to mineralisation at Blue Rose and further analysis is planned to determine the control on exo-skarn mineralisation.

Neptune Rose

  • Is interpreted to be hosted within skarn mineralisation.
  • Assessment of the structural vs stratigraphic controls on mineralisation will be assessed during future drilling.

Black Baccara

  • Is interpreted to be a sulphide rich halo around a magnetic low core.

Assessment of Geological survey hyperspectral data from nearby “near miss” diamond holes indicate the metamorphic gradient and spectral responses anticipated from a porphyry system.

Anabama Hill

    Netley Hill

      Drillhole Information

      • A summary of all information material to the understanding of the exploration results including a tabulation of the following information for all Material drill holes:
        • easting and northing of the drill hole collar
        • elevation or RL (Reduced Level – elevation above sea level in metres) of the drill hole collar
        • dip and azimuth of the hole
        • down hole length and interception depth
        • hole length.
      • If the exclusion of this information is justified on the basis that the information is not Material and this exclusion does not detract from the understanding of the report, the Competent Person should clearly explain why this is the case.
      • Drilling results are being assessed on the migration of data to the Cobra drillhole database.
      • Historic drill results reflective of the grades and widths expected of the Blue Rose prospect.
      • Reporting of these results will be included at the completion of the data migration and review.
      • Collar table presented in Appendix 1.

      Data aggregation methods

      • In reporting Exploration Results, weighting averaging techniques, maximum and/or minimum grade truncations (eg cutting of high grades) and cut-off grades are usually Material and should be stated.
      • Where aggregate intercepts incorporate short lengths of high grade results and longer lengths of low grade results, the procedure used for such aggregation should be stated and some typical examples of such aggregations should be shown in detail.
      • The assumptions used for any reporting of metal equivalent values should be clearly stated.
      • Historic grade intercepts as length weighted averages with downhole lengths reported, appropriate for this stage of drilling.
      • Where core loss occurred within mineralised intervals, the core loss was given the weighted average grade of the samples immediately above and below.
      • No top cutting of grades has been included.
      • No metal equivalent values reported.

      Relationship between mineralisation widths and intercept lengths

      • These relationships are particularly important in the reporting of Exploration Results.
      • If the geometry of the mineralisation with respect to the drill hole angle is known, its nature should be reported.
      • If it is not known and only the down hole lengths are reported, there should be a clear statement to this effect (eg ‘down hole length, true width not known’).
      • Downhole intercept lengths have been reported and are expected to be greater than true length.
      • Angled drilling has typically been dipping 60 degrees to the south with the mineralisation interpreted to be sub vertical at Blue Rose.
      • Diamond drill holes were variably angled to assess target areas as required and all drilled between 60-65 degrees dip.
      • Drilling at Anabama Hill and Netley Hill are in various orientations as this is first pass drilling to generate multi-element geochemistry.

      Diagrams

      • Appropriate maps and sections (with scales) and tabulations of intercepts should be included for any significant discovery being reported These should include, but not be limited to a plan view of drill hole collar locations and appropriate sectional views.
      • Relevant diagrams have been included in the announcement.
      • Exploration results are not being reported for existing mineral resources.
      • Drilling is aimed at extending known mineralisation and defining new mineral resources.

      Balanced reporting

      • Where comprehensive reporting of all Exploration Results is not practicable, representative reporting of both low and high grades and/or widths should be practiced to avoid misleading reporting of Exploration Results.
      • Historic results are being assessed during the data migration to the Cobra drillhole database.
      • See main body text and tables.

      Other substantive exploration data

      • Other exploration data, if meaningful and material, should be reported including (but not limited to): geological observations; geophysical survey results; geochemical survey results; bulk samples – size and method of treatment; metallurgical test results; bulk density, groundwater, geotechnical and rock characteristics; potential deleterious or contaminating substances.
      • Geological observations and analytical results (significant intersections) from previous programs have already being reported in previous announcements.
      • No results are being reported in this release.  This release is providing an update on visual results that are considered material to the market.

      Further work

      • The nature and scale of planned further work (eg tests for lateral extensions or depth extensions or large-scale step-out drilling).
      • Diagrams clearly highlighting the areas of possible extensions, including the main geological interpretations and future drilling areas, provided this information is not commercially sensitive.
      • Slimline AC/RC and conventional RC drill programs at Blue Rose, Neptune Rose, Anabama Hill and Netley Hill have commenced and are scheduled for completion in November 2026.
      • Follow up diamond drilling at Blue Rose is expected to occur in the near future.
      • A detailed aerial drone magnetic survey is expected to be completed over the Blue Rose and surrounding prospects.

23 November 2026

Cascade Studio AI plc

("Cascade" or the "Company")

Executive Role Changes

Cascade Studio AI plc (AQSE: CASC), the AI-native production platform built for filmmakers, creators, agencies and brands, announces changes to the executive roles of Simon Windsor and Darren Hopkins following completion of the Company’s acquisition of Cascade Holdings Ltd. on 9 October 2026.

Simon, a co-founder and CEO of Cascade’s operating business, will now serve as CEO of the Company, continuing to lead its strategic direction and commercial development, including overseeing strategic partnerships, brand and product marketing and the creative studio.

Darren Hopkins, who previously served as Chief Executive Officer of the Company whilst it was an acquisition vehicle and led the acquisition process, will assume the role of Chief Financial Officer ("CFO") of the Company, reverting to the position he previously held within the operating business. Darren will also continue to oversee future M&A opportunities and investor relations for the Company.

Both Simon and Darren remain executive directors of the Company, with no change to the composition of the Board.

Commenting on the Executive Role Changes, Dominic Wheatley, Non-Executive Chairman of Cascade Studio AI, said: “Following completion of the acquisition, Simon and Darren's roles at Company level now reflect their previous responsibilities within the operating business. We believe we have the necessary blend of skills and experience to capitalise on the significant growth opportunities we see ahead.

“We believe Cascade's platform will reshape who can take a great story and scale this as a high-quality professional-grade film, series, or micro-drama. Our commercial pipeline is rapidly building, and we look forward to updating the market on our early progress in due course.”

Outcome of the Resolutions

Accordingly:

The Board notes the strong level of support for each of the resolutions and believes that these approvals provide the Company with the flexibility to execute its disciplined capital allocation framework.

About B HODL:

B HODL is the first UK-listed company founded for Bitcoin accumulation and revenue generation. The Company operates a treasury-led strategy, deploying its Bitcoin holdings to power the Lightning Network and generate sustainable revenues from routing fees and liquidity provision. With a world-class team and a Bitcoin-only focus, B HODL aims to become the leading British Bitcoin company, giving investors transparent exposure to the growth of Bitcoin as both a strategic asset and a global financial standard.

Important Notice

The Company intends to hold treasury reserves and surplus cash in Bitcoin. This is a type of cryptocurrency or cryptoasset. Whilst the Board of Directors of the Company considers holding cryptocurrencies to be in the best interests of the Company, the Board remains aware that the financial regulator in the UK (the Financial Conduct Authority or FCA) considers investment in cryptocurrencies to be high risk. At the outset, it is important to note that an investment in the Company is not an investment in cryptocurrencies, either directly or by proxy, and shareholders will have no direct access to the Company's holdings. However, the Board of Directors consider cryptocurrencies to be an appropriate store of value and potential growth and therefore appropriate for the Company's reserves. Accordingly, the Company is and intends to continue to be materially exposed to cryptocurrencies. Such an approach is innovative, and the Board of Directors wish to be clear and transparent with prospective and actual investors in the Company on the Company's position in this regard.

The Company is neither authorised nor regulated by the FCA, and the purchase of certain cryptocurrencies is generally unregulated in the UK. As with most other investments, the value of cryptocurrencies can go down as well as up, and therefore the value of the Company's cryptocurrencies holdings can fluctuate. The Company may not be able to realise its cryptocurrencies holdings for the same as it paid to acquire them or even for the value the Company currently ascribes to its cryptocurrencies positions due to market movements. Neither the Company nor investors in the Company's shares are protected by the UK's Financial Ombudsman Service or the Financial Services Compensation Scheme.

Nevertheless, the Board has taken the decision to invest in cryptocurrencies, and in doing so is mindful of the special risks cryptocurrencies present to the Company's financial position. These risks include (but are not limited to): (i) the value of cryptocurrencies can be highly volatile, with value dropping as quickly as it can rise. Investors in cryptocurrencies must be prepared to lose all money invested in cryptocurrencies; (ii) the cryptocurrencies market is largely unregulated. There is a risk of losing money due to risks such as cyber-attacks, financial crime and counterparty failure; (iii) the Company may not be able to sell its cryptocurrencies at will. The ability to sell cryptocurrencies depends on various factors, including the supply and demand in the market at the relevant time. Operational failings such as technology outages, cyber-attacks and commingling of funds could cause unwanted delay; and (iv) cryptoassets are characterised in some quarters by high degrees of fraud, money laundering and financial crime. ACCELER8 VENTURES PLC

Hui10 expansion into Yunnan Province

Acceler8 Ventures Plc (LSE: AC8, “AC8” or the “Company”) is pleased to announce that its principal operating business, Hui10 Inc. (“Hui10”) has entered into agreements with Yunnan Sports Lottery to roll out

Sports Lottery+ and UGO Scratch in Yunnan Province from November 2026.

Regional rollout progressing

Yunnan represents the eighth province where Hui10 is operating Sports Lottery+, joining Hebei, Shanxi, Inner Mongolia, Jiangxi, Jiangsu, Henan and Shandong. Additionally, Yunnan represents the fourth province to rollout UGO Scratch, alongside Shanxi, Inner Mongolia and Jiangxi.

Yunnan had over 46 million residents at the end of 2025 and recorded c. RMB 25 billion in total lottery sales in 2025 from almost 8,000 Sports Lottery shops. Across all eight provinces Hui10 is expanding into markets with a combined population of over 500 million, where annual Lottery sales total c. RMB 210 billion across more than 90,000 Lottery shops

Connected Lottery Shops roll out on target

The Company remains on target to achieve over 20,000 connected Lottery Shops to Lucky World by the end of December 2026 and as at 19 November 2026, had connected 16,717 Lottery Shops to Lucky World, up 3,066 since 30 September 2026. Total registered users grew to over 1.9 million, up 0.2 million from September 2026, and on target to achieve the year-end target of over 2.0 million.

Sports Lottery+ retailer and customer proposition

Sports Lottery+ allows participating shops to use Hui10’s dedicated payment collection service, transaction records and customer management tools to simplify administration and strengthen customer relationships. Lucky World connected shops also benefit from the wider Sports Lottery+ proposition which includes real-time payment settlement and the opportunity to qualify for payments free from transaction fees.

Customers earn loyalty points, known as Love Beans, on their lottery purchases, and can redeem them as discounts on Lucky World merchandise and services. The cash portion of these merchandise purchases and subscriptions also earns Lucky Beans. Customers can redeem Lucky Beans for merchandise or Lottery HongBao, which they can use to play the lottery at Lucky World connected Lottery Shops. This links existing lottery play

with shopping, rewards and return visits within the Lucky World Lottery ecosystem.

For Hui10, the commercial objective is twofold: to generate revenue from lottery sales, and to turn the daily lottery customers of connected Lottery Shops into registered, then active Lucky World users, who generate

merchandise sales revenue.

Daniel Levine, Chief Executive Officer of AC8, said

“The Yunnan agreement extends our rollout into another substantial lottery market. UGO Scratch gives us a significant opportunity to place scratchcard sales points in almost any area of everyday consumer activity, subject to retailer and location approval. Lucky World has added more than 3,000 connected Lottery Shops

since the end of September and is focused and on track to deliver the year-end target of over 20,000.”

23 November 2026

ATC Music Group plc

("ATC", the "Company" and, together with its subsidiaries, the "Group")

Agreement to acquire One Media iP Limited,

proposed equity fundraising of up to £3.1 million,

new conditional £100 million acquisition facility

and appointment of Managing Director of ATC Rights 1 Ltd

Completing the Group's end-to-end artist services platform with rights ownership and distribution

The board of directors (the "Directors" or the "Board") of ATC Music Group plc (AIM: ATC), the independent music company providing an end-to-end music services platform spanning talent management, live touring, merchandising, e-commerce and digital engagement, is pleased to announce that ATC has agreed to acquire the entire issued share capital of One Media iP Limited ("One Media") from One Media iP Group plc (“OMIP”) (the "Acquisition").

The Acquisition will bring music rights ownership and digital distribution into the Group for the first time at scale, completing ATC's full suite of artist services.

The Board is also pleased to announce the appointment of Steve Clark as Managing Director of ATC Rights 1 Ltd (“ATC Rights”), a new wholly-owned subsidiary of the Company which will hold the Group's rights assets including those to be acquired as part of the Acquisition, and the securing of a new conditional acquisition facility of up to £100 million to fund further investment in music rights.

In addition, ATC is proposing to raise up to £3.1 million (before expenses) by way of a placing and subscription of up to 1,799,879 new ordinary shares of £0.01 each in the Company (“Ordinary Shares”) at £1.70 per share (the “Issue Price”), subject to completion of the Acquisition (the “Fundraising”). The Fundraising is intended to be undertaken as follows:

  • a placing of new Ordinary Shares (“Placing Shares”) at the Issue Price (the “Placing”) by way of an accelerated bookbuild (the “Bookbuild”) which will commence immediately following the release of this announcement in accordance with the terms and conditions set out in the Appendix; and
  • direct subscriptions with the Company for new Ordinary Shares (“Subscription Shares”) at the Issue Price (the “Subscription”).

Allenby Capital Limited (“Allenby Capital”) is acting as sole bookrunner and broker and Ocean Wall Ltd (“Ocean Wall”) is acting as placing agent (together, the “Placing Agents”) in connection with the Placing.

The Company decided to utilise a Capital Access Window pursuant to rule 40 of the AIM Rules for Companies and, accordingly, trading in the Ordinary Shares on AIM was suspended with effect from 7.30 a.m. on 11 November 2026. The Company expects to announce the outcome of the Fundraising later today, following which trading in the Ordinary Shares is expected to resume.

Highlights

  • One Media is a UK-based digital music rights owner, licensee, publisher and distributor with a diversified catalogue of over 400,000 music and related assets and rights, including master recordings, composition rights and producer royalties, distributed to over 600 digital stores globally including Apple Music, YouTube, Amazon and Spotify.
  • The Acquisition will add asset ownership and distribution to the Group's existing representation, services and events capabilities and complete its end-to-end artist services platform.
  • The Acquisition is expected to be immediately earnings enhancing and will establish Rights as a fourth reporting segment of material scale in the Group alongside Representation, Services and Events.
  • One Media generated revenue of £4.8 million for the year ended 31 October 2025.
  • Total consideration for the Acquisition is approximately £15.0 million in cash (the "Consideration") subject to customary completion accounts adjustments for cash, debt and working capital and a leakage adjustment, of which £1.0 million will be applied by OMIP in subscription for new Ordinary Shares, subject to completion of the Acquisition, at £1.72 per share (the “OMIP Subscription Price”).
  • The Acquisition is conditional on, amongst other things, the approval of OMIP's shareholders at a general meeting of OMIP expected to be held on 11 December 2026 (the “OMIP GM”), for which irrevocables to vote in favour have been obtained from shareholders representing approximately 32 per cent. of OMIP’s issued share capital. The Fundraising is conditional on, amongst other things, completion of the Acquisition.
  • The majority of the Consideration (£12 million) will be funded from a new conditional £100 million acquisition facility (the "Facility") provided by funds managed by Corrum Capital Management LLC (“Corrum Capital”), a US-based specialist lender to the music, entertainment and sports sectors, and £2 million from the Fundraising proceeds.
  • The Facility is intended to support further acquisitions of music rights and catalogues by ATC without necessarily requiring additional equity funding at the plc level.
  • The Company intends to raise up to £3.1 million (before expenses) through the Fundraising, which will be applied in part towards the Consideration (in respect of approximately £2m of the proceeds) and Acquisition costs. A further announcement will be made regarding the result of the Fundraising following the close of the Bookbuild.
  • Steve Clark, formerly Global Chief Operating Officer of Round Hill Music and a two-decade veteran of Warner Chappell Music, will join the Group as Managing Director of ATC Rights to lead the segment and manage the acquired assets

Adam Driscoll, CEO of ATC, commented:

"The acquisition of One Media completes the platform we have been building for the past five years. ATC now represents artists, services their commercial lives, promotes and produces their live work, and, with One Media, will own and distribute rights. We believe that no other independent music company offers that full suite under one roof.

"Combined with the fan data capabilities we acquired with Push and Cirkay, we believe we can increase the profitability of the catalogue beyond what it generates today.

"We are delighted that Steve Clark is joining us to lead ATC Rights. Steve brings extensive experience in global rights operations with a deep understanding of how to manage and grow music catalogues. With a conditional £100 million facility now in place, the Group has access to capital to build Rights into a segment of real scale.”

Steve Clark, Managing Director of ATC Rights, commented:

"ATC's integrated model is the most compelling platform in independent music today. The opportunity to build a rights business that sits alongside world-class management, live and fan engagement capabilities is unique, and I am looking forward to getting started."

Jonathan Mandle, Chief Investment Officer of Corrum Capital, commented:

“ATC’s position at the centre of its artists’ careers gives it a real advantage in sourcing and managing music rights. We are delighted to support the acquisition of One Media IP and look forward to growing the facility alongside ATC.”
