Notes to Editors

ATC Music Group plc is an independent music company operating internationally with strong business focus in the key commercial areas of music artist's business. The Group encompasses direct artist representation in the form of management and live representation, merchandising, music promotion, livestreaming, fan engagement, rights ownership and distribution and a range of other music services. The Group is headquartered in London, with offices in the key industry hubs of Los Angeles and New York, and also in Europe.

The Group's key businesses are structured into segments that reflect the growing range of the Group's activities:

  • Representation – artist management and live representation (ATC Management – Europe and USA, Raw Power Management, Real Life Management, ROAM)
  • Services – merchandising and e-commerce, promotion, placement and technology solutions (Sandbag, Circa, Push, Cirkay, Driift)
  • Events – venue ownership, production and promotion of live events (ATC Experience, Joy Entertainment Group, ATC LiveX)
  • Rights– ownership, administration and distribution of music rights (ATC Rights, One Media (upon completion of the Acquisition), Polyphonic, Easy Life Group)

For more information see: www.atcmusicgroup.com

DETAILS OF THE ACQUISITION AND FUNDRAISING

Details of One Media

One Media is a company incorporated in England and Wales in 2005 and a wholly-owned subsidiary of OMIP, which is quoted on AIM. One Media is a digital music rights owner, licensee, publisher and distributor. Its catalogue of over 400,000 music and related assets and rights includes master recordings of music, video and spoken word, composition rights and producer and writer royalties across genres from classical to country, soul and pop. The portfolio includes income from composition rights associated with recordings by Country Music Hall of Fame inductee Don Williams, producer royalties from Heatwave’s “Boogie Nights” and Culture Club’s “Karma Chameleon”, and master recording rights to Evelyn Thomas’s number one hit “High Energy”. It also includes rights in recordings by platinum-certified Spanish rock band Mägo de Oz, as well as rights in recordings from Point Classics, Locomotive and Entertain Me.

One Media makes its content available through more than 600 digital stores worldwide and operates over 20 YouTube channels as a certified partner, and its music is widely licensed for synchronisation in film, television, gaming and advertising.

In addition, One Media has an established royalty ingestion and accounting platform, whereby software utilised automates the collection, reconciliation and distribution of royalty income.

One Media is the only operating subsidiary of OMIP. For the financial year ended 31 October 2025,  One Media recorded revenue of £4.8 million and profit before tax of £0.9 million (£1.9 million before intercompany charges with OMIP), and gross assets at 31 October 2025 were £13.6 million.

Background and rationale for the Acquisition

The Group's strategy is to build a fully integrated, data-led artist services business that captures and enhances value across every stage of an artist's commercial life. Over the past five years ATC has assembled representation (management and live agency), services (merchandising, e-commerce, digital marketing and fan engagement technology) and events (venues, promotion and production). Ownership of rights, and the ability to distribute and monetise those rights directly, is the remaining pillar.

For ATC, the Acquisition, on completion, will deliver a resilient, high-margin earnings base which has historically required limited ongoing capital expenditure.The One Media catalogues have delivered predictable, resilient cash flows diversified across a number of catalogues and revenue streams.

The Board believes that rights ownership is a natural extension of the Group's model. Catalogue income is generally recurring in nature and not directly dependent on touring activity, which the Board believes provides a counterbalance to the seasonality of the Group's live-weighted revenues. One Media's distribution infrastructure, digital store relationships and YouTube network can be made available to artists across the Group's management and agency rosters, and the Group's fan data and engagement platform, strengthened by the acquisition of Push and Cirkay earlier this year, can be applied to increase the discoverability and earnings of the acquired catalogue.

Future growth of the Group

ATC's edge is its access to artists. ATC has spent over two decades building the relationships and infrastructure that, in the Board’s view, many funds seek to replicate through placement agents and intermediaries. The Group works directly with more than 900 artists across management, live booking, touring, merchandising and D2C, which provides origination of catalogue opportunities.

Following completion of the One Media acquisition, ATC will develop a three-tier value creation model: passive base case -which will reflect the status quo of revenue generation of assets acquired, administrative recovery -which will reflect operational and commercial efficiencies to maximise passive revenue, and active cultural activation. Hamlet Hail to the Thief, ATC Experience’s debut production, shows active cultural activation in practice, giving historic copyrights, which ATC does not own, meaningful new life. The Board believes that investing in rights alongside the artist, through partial ownership (10–50%), helps preserve the relationship on which subsequent activation depends.

Appointment of Managing Director, ATC Rights

Steve Clark will join the Group as Managing Director of ATC Rights, a non-board role, with effect from 1 December 2026. He will lead the Rights segment, oversee the integration and management of the One Media catalogue, and drive the Group's programme of further rights acquisitions.

Steve brings more than 35 years of experience in music rights management across both major and independent publishers. From 2020 until 2026 he was Global Chief Operating Officer of Round Hill Music, the New York-headquartered independent music company and one of the largest independent rights holders in the world, where he was responsible for publishing and label operations, rights administration, licensing, copyright and royalty collection across its offices in New York, Los Angeles, Nashville and London. Prior to Round Hill, he spent over two decades at Warner Chappell Music, joining as Head of Copyright and rising to Executive Vice President, Global Operations, where he led the build and global rollout of the company's contracts, copyright and royalty platform along with a client portal and app, available in many local languages. He began his career in print music at International Music Publications, where he became head of production, copyright and licensing.

Steve has served on the boards of the UK’s Music Publishers Association (MPA), the International Confederation of Music Publishers (ICMP) and the International Music Publishers Association (IMPA) and is a board adviser to music recognition technology company Audoo. He holds a music degree from the University of Liverpool.

Principal terms of the Acquisition

ATC, through its wholly-owned subsidiary ATC Rights 1 Limited (“ATC Rights”), has agreed to acquire the entire issued share capital of One Media from OMIP for cash consideration of approximately £15.0 million, subject to customary adjustments for cash, debt, working capital and leakage. £12.0 million will be funded from the Facility and £2.0 million from the proceeds of the Fundraising, with £1.0 million of the Consideration to be applied by OMIP, subject to completion of the Acquisition, in subscribing for new Ordinary Shares (the “OMIP Subscription Shares”).

The Acquisition is being undertaken pursuant to a share purchase agreement between OMIP, the Company (as guarantor), One Media and ATC Rights (the “Acquisition Agreement”). The Company has irrevocably and unconditionally guaranteed ATC Rights’ payment and performance obligations under the Acquisition Agreement. Completion of the Acquisition is conditional on certain conditions being fulfilled, including i) the approval of OMIP shareholders pursuant to Rule 15 of the AIM Rules for Companies, to be sought at a general meeting expected to be held on 11 December 2026 (the “OMIP GM”); ii) the novation to One Media of OMIP’s licence of the Record Maestro royalty accounting software from Vistex (UK) Limited, or the grant of a replacement licence on substantially the same terms, such condition which may be waived by ATC Rights; iii) the delivery to ATC Rights of duly executed payment direction letters in relation to all of One Media’s royalty payors; and iv) OMIP delivering to ATC Rights a duly executed acknowledgement of the assignment of ATC’s rights under the Acquisition Agreement to ATC Rights’ security agent. If the conditions are not satisfied or, where applicable, waived within 30 Business Days (being 7 January 2027) of the Acquisition Agreement, the Acquisition Agreement will terminate automatically and neither the Acquisition or the Fundraising will proceed. Completion of the Acquisition is expected to occur on or around 18 December 2026 (subject to a longstop date of 7 January 2027).

The resolution to approve the disposal of One Media by OMIP requires a simple majority of votes cast at the OMIP GM. OMIP has received irrevocable undertakings in respect of, in aggregate, 71,703,195 of its ordinary shares, representing approximately 32.20 per cent. of its issued share capital.

The Fundraising is conditional on completion of the Acquisition, but the Acquisition is not conditional on completion of the Fundraising.

The Acquisition Agreement contains customary warranties, indemnities, tax protections and a completion accounts mechanism. The Company has obtained warranty and indemnity insurance of £7.5 million (the “W&I Policy”), the cost of which will be borne by OMIP. The W&I Policy contains exclusions in relation to issues identified in due diligence and indemnities included in the Acquisition Agreement, as is customary. In addition, the OMIP Subscription Shares will be held in escrow for two years as security for certain claims under the Acquisition Agreement which are not covered by the W&I Policy. OMIP has also agreed to restrictions on soliciting and competing with One Media for three years following completion of the Acquisition.

As is customary for music rights portfolios, the One Media catalogue comprises a range of owned and licensed rights and royalty interests, some of which are subject to contractual terms, renewal, termination or reversion rights. The Company has undertaken legal and financial due diligence and has sought to address identified risks through the Acquisition Agreement and Escrow arrangements, further details of which are set out below.

The Consideration

The Consideration comprises base cash consideration of approximately £15.0 million, less the cost of the W&I Policy, adjusted on a pound-for-pound basis for One Media’s cash, debt and working capital against an agreed target as at 23:59 on 31 October 2026 (the “Effective Time”), and for any agreed or determined leakage. An estimated amount will be paid at Completion, with a balancing payment following agreement or determination of the completion accounts.

ATC Rights will also pay OMIP an amount equivalent to interest at 2.5 per cent. above the Bank of England base rate on £14.0 million (less the cost of the W&I Policy) from the Effective Time to Completion, by way of adjustment to the Consideration.

OMIP has subscribed, conditional on Completion, £1.0 million for 581,395 new Ordinary Shares at the OMIP Subscription Price.

Escrow for the OMIP Subscription

The OMIP Subscription Shares, once issued, will be held in escrow for two years as security for certain claims under the Acquisition Agreement which are not covered by the W&I Policy. With the consent of the Company, ATC Rights and OMIP, the OMIP Subscription Shares may be sold through Allenby Capital, the Company’s broker, at not less than 120 per cent. of the OMIP Subscription Price (unless ATC’s share price falls below 90 per cent. of the OMIP subscription price, in which case such restriction on price shall not apply), with the proceeds remaining in escrow. OMIP will retain the right to receive dividends and exercise voting rights on the OMIP Subscription Shares while they are held in escrow.

For six months following release from escrow, OMIP will dispose of the OMIP Subscription Shares only through Allenby Capital, with a view to maintaining an orderly market, save that these restrictions will not apply to a distribution in specie to OMIP shareholders, provided that any shareholder receiving more than 5 per cent. of the OMIP Subscription Shares enters into an orderly market agreement on substantively the same terms or sells those shares only through Allenby Capital.

New acquisition facility

ATC Rights, a new wholly-owned subsidiary of the Company which will hold the Group's rights assets including those to be acquired as part of the Acquisition, has entered into a facility agreement provided by Corrum Capital to fund the acquisition of music rights and catalogues by the Group. The Facility comprises a £12.0 million committed facility, which will be drawn on completion of the Acquisition to satisfy the majority of the Consideration, together with the ability to establish further uncommitted facilities, subject to an aggregate facility cap of £100 million. Further amounts may be made available to fund future approved acquisitions, subject to lender approval and, amongst other things, applicable advance rate, valuation and financial covenant requirements. The Facility is secured over the assets of ATC Rights and the shares in ATC Rights and has a term of 60 months. Loans drawn under the Facility bear interest at 11 per cent. per annum and an exit fee of 1.75 per cent. of amounts advanced is payable on repayment or at the end of the term, subject to certain exceptions.

The Board believes that the Facility provides the Group with the opportunity to pursue a disciplined programme of rights acquisitions at scale, using asset-backed debt sized to the cash flows of the catalogues acquired without necessarily requiring additional equity funding at the plc level.

The Facility contains customary change of control provisions. In the event of a change of control of the Company, each lender under the Facility may elect to cancel its commitment and require repayment of amounts outstanding under the Facility. A change of control event will not be triggered if certain specified conditions are satisfied, including if Adam Driscoll remains in senior management of the ATC Music Group, or, if he ceases to remain in senior management, replacement senior management approved by CCM Entertainment II Holdings LLC (acting as Agent) is appointed within 90 days and remains in senior management of the ATC Music Group.  The Facility also contains customary provisions relating to the identity and compliance status of any acquirer and customary fees which are payable to the Agent.

Third ISP goes live with Catena

Home Unity becomes third UK-based ISP to commence using Dotlines’ full-service OSS/BSS software platform for telco operators

Dotlines (AIM: DOTL), a UK-based international technology group with operations across the UK and Southeast Asia spanning telecommunications, digital infrastructure, cybersecurity and financial technology, is pleased to announce that Home Unity, a premium full fibre broadband provider in the UK, has gone live with the Group’s Catena platform that provides telco operators with comprehensive, automated functionality across the customer lifecycle.

This follows the Group and Home Unity signing a five-year agreement, in March 2026, for the provision of Catena. Under the agreement, the Group will receive a monthly platform fee based on usage and, during the first year, a fixed professional services fee.

Catena is the Group’s operations support system (“OSS”) and business support system (“BSS”) software platform, which provides telco operators with full in-house functionality across the sale, build and run customer lifecycle stages from a single, automated cloud-based interface. It is designed to replace the fragmented legacy systems used by small- to medium-sized telcos, internet service providers (“ISP”) and managed service providers (“MSP”) to reduce costs, eliminate errors, increase efficiency and dramatically improve the customer experience.

Since Catena’s launch in mid-2025, the Group has secured contracts with four UK-based ISPs and a strong pipeline of further opportunities. Three of the four customers have now gone live with the platform and the fourth is expected to launch in Q1 2027.

Jaki Chowdhury, CEO of Dotlines, said: “We are delighted to have our third customer go live with our Catena platform. Catena will automate many of the complex processes that would otherwise require Home Unity’s team to work across multiple supplier platforms, which will make operations simpler for them while improving the service they can provide to their customers. We continue to have a strong pipeline of opportunities for our platform and we look forward to providing further updates on our progress in due course.”

About Dotlines

Dotlines Global Ltd (AIM: DOTL) is a UK-based international technology group operating in the telecommunications, digital infrastructure, cybersecurity and financial technology sectors. Founded in Malaysia in 2007 as a bespoke B2B software development business, it has since grown to offer a range of products, platforms and solutions for both B2B and B2C customers. Its two core areas of activity are digital content and services – principally, the Sohoj digital lifestyle platform for migrant populations in Malaysia, which has served over a million migrants from countries across Asia – and telecom products and services in the UK comprising: the Catena OSS and BSS software platform for internet service providers; Audra SME- and consumer-focused cybersecurity solutions; and the Carnival Internet full fibre broadband service.

Xiaomi's Hong Kong-listed stock rebounded in the second half of the year, rising 17% in the three months through September and more than 8% so far this quarter, thanks to strong electric-vehicle sales momentum and easing concerns about memory-chip prices. Still, shares remains well below their mid-2025 peak. Analysts said the YU7 SUV's debut last year spurred a rerating of Xiaomi into a broader EV, AI and smart-ecosystem play from a pure consumer-electronics maker.

WHAT TO WATCH:

  • MARGIN: Xiaomi's smartphone business is expected to post stronger-than-expected gross margins due to rising average selling prices, Citi analyst s wrote in a recent note. However, margin softness likely persisted at its internet segment due to lower preinstallation income caused by weaker smartphone shipments and advertisement revenue, Citi said.
  • EV SALES: Investors will watch Xiaomi's EV margin to examine profitability at the company's newest and fastest-growing business. Citi analysts estimated that Xiaomi's EV sales price averaged 226,000 yuan in the third quarter, which would translate to a roughly 23.0 billion yuan revenue contribution from EVs for the period. Segment gross margin was likely flat sequentially at 19.3%, Citi said.
  • IOT SEGMENT: As for Xiaomi's Internet-of-Things segment, revenue from China remains pressured by a high base, while the overseas ramp-up has been slower than expected, Bernstein analysts wrote in a note. The brokerage forecast revenue for the segment to drop 14% this year, reflecting weak domestic demand.

data.title: Tanzania explores railway locomotive plant as East Africa seeks stronger industrial ties
data.description:
Tanzania is exploring partnerships to establish a railway locomotive manufacturing plant as part of efforts to expand domestic industrial capacity and reduce reliance on imported manufactured goods, President Samia Suluhu Hassan has announced, according to Daily News.

Hassan made the announcement in Uganda on November 19 while attending the launch of the Double Q Automotive Assembly Plant at Nakirebe in Mpigi District alongside Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni, marking the conclusion of her two-day state visit.

She did not name a partner, location or timetable for the locomotive plant, The Chanzo reported. Daily News separately reported her as saying Tanzania was exploring cooperation with Japan's Hitachi , which manufactures train engines.

Daily News said the proposed plant would build on Tanzania's railway manufacturing efforts following the commencement of metre-gauge railway locomotive assembly at the Tanzania Railways Corporation (TRC) workshop in Pugu, Dar es Salaam, in March.

Hassan urged East African Community (EAC) member states to align their industrialisation strategies and develop complementary industries rather than compete for similar investments.

“Let us turn from being consumers of imported goods to regional production and marketing hubs. We should aspire to manufacture, assemble and produce,” she said, as quoted by Daily News.

She also called for harmonised regulations governing vehicle assembly and manufacturing to support regional value chains and encourage investment across different industrial sectors.

Museveni said pooling regional resources could strengthen manufacturing, citing Tanzania's natural gas reserves and Uganda's iron ore deposits as complementary inputs for industrial production.

“Prosperity comes from business, and business means natural resources. These countries have got different natural resources. You find that Tanzania has got gas, Uganda has got iron ore and other products. So, when you put them together, instead of using them in many fragmented ways, you do better business,” he said, according to Daily News.

Hassan praised Uganda's automotive investment, saying local assembly would reduce reliance on imported second-hand vehicles and discourage the dumping of manufactured goods in the region.

Museveni also commended Double Q Motors and its Chinese partner Sinotruk (HKEX:03808) for investing in truck assembly and welcomed the company's intention to eventually use locally produced steel in vehicle components, Daily News and The Chanzo reported.

Double Q Managing Director Lin Yu said the company, which entered Uganda in 2013, became an official Sinotruk distributor in 2017 and began assembling trucks in 2020. Its new plant has an annual capacity of 4,000 trucks and plans to expand into passenger and electric vehicles. More than 5,000 trucks have already been assembled in Uganda.

Works and Transport Minister Fred Byamukama put the investment at $30mn and said the plant directly employs more than 1,200 Ugandans, Watchdog Uganda reported.
